text:
Ah, understanding, that slippery eel! You want to grasp it, to pin it down, but it wriggles free, doesn't it? I, on the other hand, embrace the wriggle!

To truly understand a thing, you must first misunderstand it, wouldn't you say?

See, by approaching a knot of complexity with preconceptions, you blind yourself to its true nature. You must start by assuming the opposite, by embracing the absurd!

Think of a square circle, a silent scream. What is it, this paradoxical beast?

By exploring the impossible, by dancing with the nonsensical, you begin to see the edges of understanding. It's like peeling an onion, layer by layer, each one revealing a new absurdity, a new truth.

So, my friend, to understand something complex, you must first learn to laugh at it, to revel in its confusion. Only then will the fog clear, and the truth, like a mischievous sprite, will reveal itself.
